![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14220666/assets/5d88a8e80d3008450a3e807750ee0f02c9b733eca5407d7dda416ce43303ba18.png)

Which of the above could be the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's recall some of the basic properties of $y=\sqrt{x}.$

- The point $(0,0)$ lies on the graph

- Its domain is $x\in [0,\infty )$

- Its range is $y\in [0,\infty )$

- The function is increasing over its entire domain.

- As $x\to \infty $, we have $y\to \infty ,$ though it does so slowly

Of the given options, only graph III has all of the above properties. Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

choices.value: None of the given functions is the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$
